records.text: Owens said Stephen Feinberg co-founded Cerberus Capital Management in 1992, that it managed 70 billion dollars in assets, and that DynCorp entered its portfolio in 2010.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: Well, in 1992, he co-founded Cerberus Capital Management. ... Cerberus Capital Management is a fund with 70 billion AUM. That's assets that are under their management, 70 billion. ... Steven Feinberg was one half. He's a co-founder and that's why he was a controversial pick, not just because of his extraordinary wealth, but more specifically due to one particular asset which came under their management portfolio in 2010, DynCorp.

verification.notes: Official Defense and Cerberus materials confirm Feinberg co-founded Cerberus in 1992, that the firm grew to approximately 70 billion dollars in assets under his leadership, and that Cerberus affiliates completed the DynCorp acquisition in July 2010.

records.text: Owens cited reports by DynCorp investigator Kathryn Bolkovac and employee Ben Johnston alleging that DynCorp personnel in Bosnia purchased underage women and facilitated sex trafficking; Owens said both whistleblowers were fired after reporting the abuses.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: And if you also guessed that they were caught, I don't know, Candace, human sex trafficking. Plus accused of forced child prostitution and rape ... Kathryn Bolkovac, a DynCorp investigator in Bosnia, discovered that several DynCorp employees were involved in purchasing underaged women and facilitating sex trafficking. ... Another employee, Ben Johnston, filed similar reports. Both were then fired by the company

verification.notes: Congressional testimony and Human Rights Watch reporting identify Bolkovac and Johnston as DynCorp whistleblowers, describe allegations that employees purchased women and facilitated trafficking, and document their termination and later employment litigation.

records.text: Owens said Kathryn Bolkovac's book reported that trafficked underage women came from Ukraine, Croatia, Bosnia, and Romania.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: And I want to be clear because I downloaded her book over this past weekend and was speed reading through it that the trafficked underage women were coming from Ukraine, Croatia, Bosnia, and of course, Romania.

verification.notes: The cited book was identified, but no accessible passage verified this exact four-country list. Independent reporting on the same investigation consistently identifies victims from Ukraine, Moldova, and Romania; it does not conclusively verify the Croatia and Bosnia portions as stated.

records.text: Owens said NATO created the International Police Task Force as an arm of the United Nations civilian police force, and she alleged that the United Nations and DynCorp were charged with trafficking children, forcing prostitution, and covering it up.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: And in this case, it was the International Police Task Force. That was an arm of the United Nations Civilian Police Force. ... They were created by NATO. ... Except they were exactly the ones who were charged with trafficking the children, covering it up, the United Nations, DynCorp, forcing them into prostitution.

verification.notes: United Nations records directly contradict the claim that NATO created the task force: Security Council Resolution 1035 established the UN International Police Task Force. Congressional and rights reports substantiate trafficking allegations against some DynCorp and international personnel, but not the blanket formulation that the United Nations as an institution was charged with the crimes.

sources.relevance: Official record shows the UN Security Council established the International Police Task Force.

records.text: Owens said DynCorp officers accused of trafficking, forced prostitution, and rape enjoyed immunity, that military contractors were not prosecuted in foreign territories, and that DynCorp continued its U.S. government relationship without prosecution.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: Yet despite reporting that the officers were indeed at DynCorp trafficking, prostituting and raping the victims, they got to enjoy immunity. ... Military contractors don't have to suffer any prosecution in foreign territories. So in the end, DynCorp got off scot-free and just continued their relationship with the United States government.

verification.notes: Human Rights Watch found that no DynCorp employees were prosecuted in Bosnia or the United States for the documented trafficking-related cases and that international personnel had immunity in Bosnia. The categorical claim that military contractors cannot be prosecuted abroad is false; federal law and the Blackwater case demonstrate extraterritorial prosecution routes.

sources.title: Hopes Betrayed
sources.relevance: Documents immunity and the absence of trafficking prosecutions for DynCorp employees in Bosnia and the United States at that time.

records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: Now, when her movie about the scandal came out in 2010, DynCorp sold to Stephen Feinberg's Cerberus. It was owned by Cerberus for the next 10 years.

verification.notes: Cerberus announced completion of its DynCorp acquisition in July 2010, and Amentum announced completion of its acquisition from Cerberus in November 2020. This supports ownership for approximately ten years.
